summary: Specifies a simple protocol for establishing symmetric data channels between WebRTC peers, using a two-way handshake and allowing user data to be sent before the handshake completes.

eli5.summary: Two browsers agree on a message pipe with a quick hello, and can start talking right away.

questions: how are webrtc data channels established
what is the data channel establishment protocol
how do webrtc data channels get opened
why do dtls clients use even stream ids
what channel types does dcep define
subtitle: How two browsers open a named, tunable message channel inside one SCTP connection with a two-message handshake.

tldr.problem: WebRTC peers share one SCTP association over DTLS and need a simple in-band way to open many channels, each with its own reliability, ordering, priority and label.
tldr.mechanism: One peer sends a DATA_CHANNEL_OPEN message on a chosen stream, the other answers with DATA_CHANNEL_ACK on the matching stream, and the two streams together form a bidirectional data channel.
tldr.outcome: Either side can open channels without collisions because DTLS clients use even stream identifiers and DTLS servers use odd ones, and the opener can send data before the ACK arrives.

today: RFC 8832 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2021 and, per the metadata for this unit, has not been obsoleted or updated. It is the companion to RFC 8831, which describes WebRTC data channels themselves.

sections.title: Why a Channel Setup Protocol
sections.content:
The Data Channel Establishment Protocol (DCEP) gives WebRTC a simple, in-band method for opening symmetric data channels. As RFC 8831 describes, WebRTC data channels run over the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) carried inside Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS), as described in RFC 8261.

Because DCEP rides on that stack, it gets the standardized transport and security features of SCTP and DTLS without defining its own. The RFC notes DTLS 1.0, 1.2 and an upcoming 1.3 as the DTLS versions in play when it was written.
sections.eli5: Two browsers already share one big pipe. This protocol is the polite way to carve smaller labelled pipes out of it.

sections.title: Streams and Data Channels
sections.content:
The RFC defines a few terms. An association is an SCTP association. A stream is a unidirectional SCTP stream, identified by a stream identifier from 0 to 65534 (65535 is reserved because SCTP INIT and INIT-ACK chunks only allow 65535 streams to be negotiated).

A data channel is two streams with the same stream identifier, one in each direction, managed together. Every channel in the association shares a consistent set of properties: reliable or unreliable delivery (with the same level of unreliability used if unreliable), in-order or out-of-order delivery, a priority, an optional label, an optional protocol, and the streams themselves.
sections.eli5: A data channel is like two one-way pipes with the same number, one carrying messages each way, treated as a single two-way pipe.

sections.title: The Two-Way Handshake
sections.content:
The initiating peer picks a stream identifier whose incoming and outgoing streams are both unused and sends DATA_CHANNEL_OPEN on the outgoing stream. The other peer replies with DATA_CHANNEL_ACK on its corresponding outgoing stream, and then the channel is open.

DCEP messages travel on the same stream as the channel's user messages. They are told apart by the SCTP Payload Protocol Identifier (PPID), since DCEP uses a specific PPID. The opener MAY send user messages before the ACK arrives.

To avoid collisions, each side uses only even or only odd stream identifiers when opening channels. The side acting as the DTLS client MUST use even identifiers and the DTLS server MUST use odd ones. Labels are not kept unique: if both sides open a channel labeled "x" at the same time, there will be two channels labeled "x".
sections.eli5: One browser says "let us use pipe 4, here is how it works," and the other says "got it." To stop both picking the same pipe, one side only uses even numbers and the other only odd.

sections.title: The OPEN and ACK Messages
sections.content:
Every DCEP message starts with a one-byte Message Type. DATA_CHANNEL_OPEN is type 0x03 and then carries a Channel Type (1 byte), Priority (2 bytes), Reliability Parameter (4 bytes), Label Length (2 bytes), Protocol Length (2 bytes), and then the variable-length Label and Protocol, both UTF-8 strings. The label may be empty. An empty protocol means unspecified; otherwise it names a protocol from the WebSocket Subprotocol Name Registry created in RFC 6455.

The Channel Type selects reliability and ordering. For reliable types the Reliability Parameter MUST be 0 when sent and is ignored on receipt. For retransmission-limited types it is the number of retransmissions, and for timed types it is the maximum lifetime in milliseconds.

DATA_CHANNEL_ACK is just the one-byte Message Type 0x02. Receiving it tells the opener that setup is complete.
sections.eli5: The hello note says what kind of pipe you want, how important it is, and what to call it. The reply note is just a single "yes."

sections.title: Procedures and Error Handling
sections.content:
All DCEP messages MUST be sent with ordered, reliable delivery, on the same outgoing stream as the channel's user messages, and with the DCEP PPID. No other messages may use that PPID.

A receiver replies with an ACK only if the OPEN arrived on an unused stream, the stream identifier matches the peer's role, and all parameters are valid. Otherwise it MUST close the channel using the procedure in RFC 8831 and MUST NOT send an ACK. The opener sees this as an SCTP stream reset on a stream with no ACK received, and once the reset completes a new OPEN can be sent on that stream.

After sending OPEN, the sender MAY send user data right away. Until an ACK or any other message arrives, user messages MUST be sent ordered, even on an unordered channel. After that, ordered channels use ordered sends and unordered channels use unordered sends. User data on an unused stream is an error and the channel MUST be closed.
sections.eli5: If the hello is wrong or the pipe is already taken, the other side hangs up instead of saying yes. Until the first answer comes back, everything is sent in order to stay safe.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
A receiver must be prepared for DATA_CHANNEL_OPEN messages where the label and protocol fields have the maximum length of 65535 bytes. Inconsistent field lengths, unknown parameter values and violations of the odd/even rule must be handled by closing the channel. An endpoint must also be ready for the peer to open the maximum number of data channels.

DCEP itself provides no privacy, integrity or authentication. It must be used within a protocol suite that provides them, such as the one in RFC 8261. For general WebRTC considerations the RFC points to RFC 8826 and RFC 8827.
sections.eli5: Be ready for huge or weird hello notes and hang up on bad ones. The pipe itself is not secret, so it has to run inside a protected tunnel.

sections.title: IANA Registries
sections.content:
IANA renamed the existing SCTP PPID 50 from "WebRTC Control" to "WebRTC DCEP" and pointed its reference at this document. It also created a standalone "Data Channel Establishment Protocol (DCEP) Parameters" registry with two subregistries.

In the Message Types registry, 0x02 is DATA_CHANNEL_ACK, 0x03 is DATA_CHANNEL_OPEN, 0x04 to 0xfe is unassigned, and 0x00, 0x01 and 0xff are reserved (the first two because draft versions used them). New types need an RFC Required action under RFC 8126.

In the Channel Types registry the high-order bit marks unordered delivery for any new type that supports both modes. Values 0x7f and 0xff are reserved for future extensibility.
sections.eli5: IANA keeps the official list of note types and pipe types so that nobody reuses a number for a different meaning.

fields.name: Channel Type
fields.desc: Reliability and ordering of the channel.

fields.name: Reliability Parameter
fields.desc: Retransmission count or lifetime in ms; 0 for reliable types.

fields.name: Label Length
fields.desc: Length of the label in bytes.

fields.name: Protocol Length
fields.desc: Length of the protocol in bytes.

messages.label: DATA_CHANNEL_OPEN
messages.note: Sent on the chosen outgoing stream.

messages.label: User data
messages.note: May be sent before the ACK arrives.

messages.label: DATA_CHANNEL_ACK
messages.note: Sent on the stream with the same identifier.

items.label: DATA_CHANNEL_PARTIAL_RELIABLE_REXMIT
items.desc: Partially reliable, in order, limited retransmissions.

items.label: DATA_CHANNEL_PARTIAL_RELIABLE_TIMED
items.desc: Partially reliable, in order, limited lifetime.
